core: distinguishing legal form from tax classification
outOfScope: detailed corporation, LLC, and partnership doctrine

claims.claim: Common U.S. business forms include sole proprietorships, partnerships, corporations, S corporations, and LLCs; an LLC is a structure allowed by state statute.
A business structure can affect taxes, fundraising, paperwork, and personal liability, so those questions should be kept distinct in a comparison.
The SBA describes a sole proprietorship as not producing a separate business entity and a corporation as a legal entity separate from its owners.
The SBA presents liability protection for LLCs and corporations in qualified terms and notes more extensive recordkeeping, operational processes, and reporting for corporations.
The IRS states that federal tax classification of an LLC can depend on its number of members and elections, so entity form and tax treatment are separate questions.
Ownership rules, liability, taxes, and filing requirements can vary by state, so a general U.S. overview cannot resolve a specific entity decision.
